NVDA.headline: Shares slip amid AI sell-off; reports on TSMC memory base dies
NVDA.summary: NVIDIA closed at 214.13 USD, down 1.43% today and 2.38% over the month, within a 52-week range of 164.27–243.37. Reports say Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to use TSMC's 3nm process for base dies of its custom NVHBM memory, a claim not confirmed by the companies. Broader AI-led selling and questions over AI spending have weighed on tech stocks, with markets looking to a rebound and to Magnificent Seven earnings.

MSFT.headline: Shares drop 1.9% as UK regulator proposes new business software designation
MSFT.summary: Microsoft is priced at 529.05 USD, down 1.93% today, though up 6.29% over the month. The UK Competition and Markets Authority proposes designating Microsoft with Strategic Market Status in business software, which could lead to required changes to bundling, licensing and interoperability. Reports say Microsoft cut internal spending on Anthropic's Claude, and an unverified leak suggests a possible budget Xbox console.

AAPL.headline: Shares up modestly; foldable and MacBook launch reports
AAPL.summary: Apple is priced at 343.46 USD, up 0.43% today and 1.92% over the month. Reports suggest a touchscreen MacBook and OLED iPad mini could go on sale from 6 November, though Apple has not confirmed dates. Apple's foldable iPhone Duo battery data has been published, and a report says the company's Sainte-Catherine store in Bordeaux was looted during French protests. A report found teen test accounts could download nudify apps from Apple and Google stores; Apple says it has tightened guidelines.

GOOGL.headline: Shares fall 2.5%; Gemini renaming and Waymo Toronto plans
GOOGL.summary: Alphabet is priced at 340.59 USD, down 2.47% today and 1.94% over the month. Google is moving personal Gems into Skills from 17 November, and Waymo plans a driverless robotaxi service in Toronto by 2028. Gemini 4 agents reportedly completed Minecraft autonomously. A report on nudify apps accessible to teens also named Google, which says it suspended violating apps.

AMZN.headline: Shares slip 1.9%; UK cloud competition scrutiny in focus
AMZN.summary: Amazon is priced at 250 USD, down 1.87% today and 0.47% over the month. The UK Competition and Markets Authority said AWS and Microsoft could do more to remove barriers in cloud services. Anthropic, which is privately held, plans to set aside 5% of its shares for a public benefit fund, which affects no listed shares directly.

META.headline: Shares down 3.7%; No Kings account suspension and fake app reports
META.summary: Meta is priced at 709.33 USD, down 3.72% today and up 3.96% over the month. Meta said an automated system, linked to a Claude AI tool, mistakenly suspended the No Kings Instagram account before it was restored. Reports say Meta halved its Claude Code users, and a counterfeit WhatsApp app reportedly passed 500,000 downloads on Google Play. Meta's results are due on Wednesday.

AVGO.headline: No major news; shares down 4.52% today
AVGO.summary: There is no major news for Broadcom right now. The shares fell 4.52% today and are down 5.34% over one month, trading at 328.75 USD within a 52-week range of 289.96–495.

TSLA.headline: Robotaxi, merger chatter and Roadster launch in focus
TSLA.summary: Waymo plans a driverless robotaxi service in Toronto by 2028, which is a competitor development. Unconfirmed speculation about a Tesla and SpaceXAI merger has circulated on X, though nothing has been confirmed. Shares fell 2.13% today to 354.72 USD and are down 19.26% over the past year amid a broader tech selloff.

TSM.headline: Shares fall 2.3% as chip stocks extend losing streak
TSM.summary: TSMC is priced at 412.61 USD, down 2.28% today and 4.1% over the month. US semiconductor stocks have reportedly closed lower for eight straight sessions, the longest run in 16 years, amid AI revenue doubts and inflation concerns. Reports say Nvidia has asked Samsung and others to use TSMC's 3nm process for memory base dies, which is unconfirmed. China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, supported by AI-related chip exports.

SPCX.headline: Shares slip 1.7%; no major company news
SPCX.summary: There is no major news right now for Space Exploration Technologies. Shares are priced at 146.03 USD, down 1.74% today and 5.67% over the month, and sit within a 52-week range of 104.83–225.64. Recent coverage includes a general Artemis II crew account and an explainer on drive storage, neither of which is a new company development.
